claims.summary: For odd p,n>=2, the supported square-root Cauchy-Binet transfer admits the universal one-root degree bound U_tau=w_tau-sum(Gamma)-tau*n, where w_tau is the maximum weighted column-basis value of [I_(Gamma minus0)|Toeplitz(b)]. Fixing distinct old roots over F_(p^e), if the initial original minor norm has degree e*U_tau and selected cofactor norms have gcd Norm(V)^(n+1), then generic reduced cofactors have gcd1 and ell0(3,binom(n+1,2)+2)=3binom(n+1,4) over every characteristic-p field.
claims.assessment: Working proof: each nonzero transfer minor extends to a full constant-matrix column basis, giving a universal upper bound. Attaining it preserves the one-root degree of the global cofactor gcd, which has equal degrees in every root by permutation covariance. Norm coprimality excludes that divisor. Requires at least n supported input columns; the frame and successful degree condition imply U_tau>=n(n+1), so it is not an additional hypothesis; unverified rank/degree/gcd failures remain inconclusive.
claims.rationale: A source-preserving sufficient certificate combining existing cofactor symmetry and transfer with elementary maximum-weight linear-basis bounds. It is actually used to prove the missing quinary boundary; no external novelty or benchmark speedup claimed.
claims.next_action: Seek a uniform polynomial relation using every maximizing transfer contribution, not only one basis or additional prime samples.

claims.next_action: Retain the exact solved target as a control while seeking a uniform primitive-relation argument.
